title: Record that the intersection-counter engine returns the E6 64-word set.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Exhaustive finite comparison, not a new conditional exponent. On the pinned 7-generator kernel of the E6 4-frame incidence code, `research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py` at batch size 16 returns the same 64 words as the literal span. The SHA256 of the 63 positive words, as a default JSON list, is `ad4a1d101774e6c2da40cde3d097d39aa56ee5668dcdca858513c5fec3578215`.

The selected conditional exponent stays `781451/250000000`. This package does not change `certificates/selected-result.json`. The priorities page on this base still prints the older PR #5599 decimal; the selected record is the value used here.

The domain is the 128-word F2 span of the seven generators below. A literal doubling lists every codeword. Batch size 16 puts all seven generators in one lane block, so the engine's high-offset loop runs once. The observed stream is 64 distinct words and equals the weight-at-most-16 subset: zero and 63 words of weight 16. That is an exhaustive census of this finite input at this batch size. It does not decide another batch size or another code, and a faster runtime is not the claim.

## Task and overlap

Base `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8, task card `replay-runtime`. Scope status is **refined**. The card asks for a measured speedup that keeps coverage. Revision 8 requires the sets to be compared before a faster replay counts as the same coverage. The merged package `research/e7-intersection-counters` (Nick Petalas, `a341471127ab570dcca1fa3ee1deaded3c5ca496`) times the complete E7 consumer and states that other codes are outside its claim. The predecessor comparison on fork commit `f770aeb71385a5e14b38ca6e1e0df6cccde6c646` (`cursor/replay-coverage-gap-3fad`) binds `low_weight_words` on this E6 code and leaves the intersection-counter engine unrun.

`scripts/find_overlap.py` on 2026-11-10 searched `ad4a1d101774e6c2`, `e6-frame-code-lane-coverage`, and `intersection-counter engine`, including closed pull requests. Coverage: 8919 local notes at this base, complete inventory; 885 open PR bodies at `2026-11-10T02:02:41Z`; 6934 discussion records at `2026-11-10T02:03:39Z`; 5530 closed PR bodies at `2026-11-10T02:04:20Z`. Zero matches. Comment bodies in that snapshot have no copy of the hash. Replies past the first 100 on comments after each discussion's first page are outside that helper's walk. The discussion-comment lookup for id 19492511 returned HTTP 404. Upstream `main` was fetched again before submission and was still `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`.

The lines are the E6 unit of `research/e6-e7-shadow-minrank-upper/WITNESSES.json`, in witness order. The 135 orthogonal 4-frames have incidence rank 29. The kernel basis with identity on free coordinates `(0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 20)` is:

```text
6591703721
6306835114
13904919564
45813124144
28344004800
68452089600
68718428160
```

Two of those generators have weight 20, so they lie in the span and outside the returned set. Width 36, weight bound 16, batch size 16. A D6 or P112 punctured frame is a different code and is outside this comparison. The 27-dimensional E7 census is not replayed.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library, from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/e6-intersection-counter-support --check-only
python3 -I -B research/e6-intersection-counter-support/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/e6-intersection-counter-support/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/e6-intersection-counter-support
```

Direct normal and optimized receipts are byte-identical. The registered runner prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/e6-intersection-counter-support outcome=completed`. `scripts/check_research_commit.py` passed for `ac733580dc8eccea54935b82a73be9bf6a72c379`.

The engine call is `low_weight_words` in `research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py`, with `population_planes` and `at_most` injected from `research/e7-bitsliced-exhaustion/binary.py`. Those helpers are the engine's weight routines. The comparison does not call that file's enumerator; a direct call with the injected keywords raises `TypeError`. A repeated generator raises `ValueError` with the engine message `dependent generators`. Dropping the least positive word changes the set and the hash.

The census is finite and complete for this span at batch size 16. It is not a heuristic sample and not a theorem about other inputs. The selected-baseline script, the E7 census, Lean, Docker, and any timing harness were not run.

## Credit

The E6 lines and A2 anchors are Nick Petalas's shadow witness. The intersection-counter engine is Nick Petalas's `research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py`. The injected population and threshold routines are Ali Romman's PR #5729. The 64-word set and the support hash are the predecessor comparison on `cursor/replay-coverage-gap-3fad`.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0. No independent human review and no formal-kernel acceptance are claimed.

## Open next questions

1. Does the same set equality hold at another legal batch size, for example 8? Batch size changes the lane split. First rerun this comparison with `batch_bits` 8 and the same seven generators, weight bound, and support hash. Nothing mathematical blocks that rerun. This package stops after batch size 16.

2. Can this opt-in engine be installed at a caller that consumes the E6 4-frame code, with regenerated source pins? Set equality on one code leaves that replacement untouched. The first step is the installation and source-bound compatibility check already stated by `research/e7-intersection-counters`. This comparison does not regenerate consumer pins.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The predecessor hash lives on a fork branch and was absent from the upstream discussion snapshot, including a 404 for the cited comment id. Searching fork branches for a cited hash, when the discussion comment cannot be read, would make this handoff easier to find. Feedback thread: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
